title: Further statistics: estimation, Poisson and Markov chains
summary: Designing reliable data collection, non-linear regression, linear combinations of random variables, the central limit theorem, confidence intervals, the Poisson distribution, further hypothesis tests and Markov chains.

keyterms.definition: A measurement is reliable if it gives consistent results when repeated.
A measurement is valid if it measures what it is intended to measure.
R²: the proportion of variation in y explained by the model.
SSres = Σ(observed − predicted)²; least-squares regression minimises it.
A sample statistic whose expected value equals the population parameter, e.g. s²ₙ₋₁.
For large n (n ≥ 30), the sample mean is approximately N(μ, σ²/n) whatever the population.
A range of values likely to contain a population parameter, at a stated confidence level.
X ~ Po(m): number of events in a fixed interval at a constant mean rate m; mean = variance = m.
Rejecting H₀ when it is true.
Not rejecting H₀ when it is false.
A matrix of probabilities of moving between states; each column sums to 1.
The long-term state vector s with Ts = s.

questions.prompt: A test that gives the same results when repeated under the same conditions is:
questions.explanation: Reliability is about consistency; validity is about measuring the right thing.
Repeat the test and compare the two sets of results.

questions.text: R² = 0.81 means 81% of the variation in y is ___ by the model.
questions.explanation: R² describes fit, not causation.

questions.prompt: A least-squares regression model minimises:
questions.explanation: Squaring stops positive and negative residuals cancelling.

questions.prompt: An observed value is 12 and the model predicts 10.5. Find the residual.
questions.explanation: Residual = observed − predicted.

questions.statement: For a linear model, R² equals r².
questions.explanation: For non-linear models, use the R² from the GDC.

questions.prompt: Two models fitted to the same data have SSres = 4.2 and SSres = 9.8. Which fits better?
questions.explanation: A smaller sum of squared residuals means the points are closer to the model.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: measures what it claims to measure
two equivalent versions give similar results

questions.explanation: Parallel forms is a reliability check; criterion-related validity is a validity check.

items: Choose candidate models from its shape and the context
Fit each model with the GDC
Compare R² or SSres and the context
questions.explanation: The best model fits well and makes sense in context.

questions.prompt: Exponential regression gives y = 3.1 × 1.2ˣ. Predict y when x = 5.

lessons.title: Linear combinations, CLT and confidence intervals

questions.prompt: E(X) = 5. Find E(3X − 2).
Var(X) = 4. Find Var(3X − 2).
questions.explanation: Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X); adding a constant does not change spread.

questions.text: A sample of n = 10 has variance s²ₙ = 9. The unbiased estimate of the population variance is ___.

questions.statement: By the central limit theorem, the mean of a large sample is approximately normal even if the population is not.
questions.explanation: A guideline is n ≥ 30.

questions.prompt: A population has σ = 12. Find the standard deviation of the mean of samples of size 36.
x̄ = 50, σ = 10 and n = 25. Find a 95% confidence interval for μ.
Raising the confidence level from 90% to 99% makes the interval:
questions.explanation: More confidence needs a wider range.

questions.prompt: For independent X and Y, match each quantity.
questions.explanation: Variances add even when the variables are subtracted.

questions.prompt: If σ is unknown and the sample is small, a confidence interval for μ uses:
questions.explanation: The t-distribution allows for estimating σ from the sample.

questions.prompt: Put the steps for finding a confidence interval in order.
items: Check the conditions (normal population or large n)
Find the sample mean and standard deviation
questions.explanation: Interpret it as a range of plausible values for μ.

lessons.title: Poisson, further tests and Markov chains

questions.prompt: X ~ Po(3). Find P(X = 0).

questions.text: For X ~ Po(m), the mean and the variance both equal ___.
questions.explanation: Mean ≈ variance in data suggests a Poisson model.

questions.prompt: Calls arrive at a mean rate of 3 per hour. Find P(at most 4 calls in 2 hours).
questions.explanation: Scale the rate: X ~ Po(6), so poissoncdf(6, 4) ≈ 0.285.

questions.statement: The sum of two independent Poisson variables is also Poisson.
questions.explanation: Po(a) + Po(b) = Po(a + b).

questions.prompt: A Type I error is:
options: not rejecting H₀ when it is false
rejecting H₀ when it is true
questions.explanation: P(Type I error) equals the significance level for a continuous test statistic.

questions.prompt: A Type II error is:
options: rejecting H₀ when it is true
not rejecting H₀ when it is false
questions.explanation: It is a missed real effect.

questions.prompt: T = [0.8 0.3; 0.2 0.7] (columns sum to 1) for states A, B. Find the steady state.
questions.explanation: Solve Ts = s: 0.2a = 0.3b with a + b = 1, so a = 0.6.
